meta.description:
Imagine standing in a fifty-mile strip of land where you could theoretically commit a crime and walk away completely free. It sounds like a movie plot, but this place actually exists inside Yellowstone National Park. It is called the Zone of Death. Because of a bizarre constitutional loophole, if you commit a crime in this Idaho section of the park, the government might not be able to legally prosecute you. The law says you have a right to a jury from both the state and the district where the crime happened. But nobody lives in this overlap zone. No jury means no trial, and no trial means no conviction. It is a terrifying legal blind spot that Congress still hasn't fixed. Would you ever camp here, or are you staying far away? Follow for more wild secrets.
